newsitem.title: SPAIN: Two Basque journalists charged with Spain bombing.
newsitem.headline: Two Basque journalists charged with Spain bombing.

text.p: Two journalists with the radical Basque daily Egin appeared in a Spanish high court accused with bombing offices in Salvatierra in the Basque province of Vizcaya, according to court documents released on Monday.

Judge Gomez de Liano accused Fernando Alonso Abad and Andoni Murga of responsibility for the August 15 bombing of the offices. They were charged with belonging to an armed band, destruction, and storing arms and explosives.

He said both men belonged to ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom), which had provided them with arms and explosives to attack businesses which refused to pay extortion money, the so-called "revolutionary tax".
They had been arrested in August and were both imprisoned after the judge's order pending 3.5 million pesetas ($23,600) bail.

Police found arms and explosives in Alonso Abad's house and several lists of extortion victims in his desk at Egin. Egin is the usual mouthpiece for ETA separatists, who have killed 800 people since starting a violent drive for Basque independence in 1968.
